questions.stem: Let A = {1, 2, 3, 4} and B = {3, 4, 5}. What is A − B?
questions.explain: A − B keeps the elements of A that are not in B: 1 and 2.

questions.stem: In a class of 40 students, 25 like maths, 20 like physics and 10 like both. How many like at least one of the two?
questions.explain: Adding 25 and 20 counts the 10 who like both twice, so 25 + 20 − 10 = 35.

options: p is false and q is true
p is true and q is true
p is true and q is false
p is false and q is false
questions.explain: A promise “if p then q” is broken only when p happens and q does not.
De Morgan: negating an AND gives an OR of the negations, so ¬(p ∧ q) ≡ ¬p ∨ ¬q.

questions.stem: Which is the negation of “every bird can fly”?
questions.explain: One bird that cannot fly breaks the claim, and that is exactly “some bird cannot fly”.
